messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testGetStringInconsistentRecord()` triggers an IllegalArgumentException when trying to access a record value by a key "fourth" which apparently does not exist in the header mapping. The current bug report states that the CSVRecord class does not verify whether the size of the header mapping matches the number of values in a record.

Analyzing the code snippet of `CSVRecord.get(String)` shows it tries to lookup the index of the column name in the mapping and then access the corresponding index in the values array. However, there is no check to confirm that the index is within the range of the values array length. If the mapping size is larger than the values array, this can lead to an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException as described in the bug report.

The `CSVRecord` constructor simply assigns the values and mapping without validating their lengths. The `CSVParser.nextRecord()` method reads tokens and compiles the record values array and then creates the CSVRecord using a mapping stored in `headerMap`. This mapping apparently can have length inconsistent with the values array.

The lack of consistent validation for length between the values array and the header mapping allows records with inconsistent states causing array index issues or unclear exceptions. The test expects an IllegalArgumentException, indicating that the API should add explicit size consistency checks in `CSVRecord` construction or access.

No recent bug reports gave hints for this failure. Hence, the root cause is the missing validation and size consistency enforcement between the header mapping and the record values array in CSVRecord management.

Next, I will suggest which method(s) to be fixed based on this reasoning.
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.get(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.<init>(java.lang.String[],java.util.Map,java.lang.String,long)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
